articles.title: UAE freezes Desi Bling star's assets
articles.text: Mumbai: The UAE anti-money laundering agency Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) is understood to have asked banks, financial institutions, and virtual asset service providers (VASPs) in the Emirates to put a temporary freeze on the accounts of Satish Sanpal, the 41-year-old Dubai-based Indian-origin businessman who stars in the Netflix docusoap series 'Desi Bling' that shows the lavish lifestyle of Sanpal and his wife Tabinda.Besides the financial services accounts and digital wallets of Satish, the FIU freezing order, issued about a fortnight ago, extends to accounts of Tabinda and companies linked to Sanpals."...you are immediately requested to freeze any funds or accounts or deposits or investments and deny access to the safe deposit boxes, and stop any financial transfers or withdrawals and inform us of any credit facilities belonging to the below mentioned names.." said the FIU communique.132795452The business entities covered in the notice are ANAX Capital Asset Management Company, ANAX Capital Financial Markets LLC, ANAX Holding FZCO, and SSB Bazaar General Trading LLC. SSB, which is said to deal in precious stones, was formed in 2015, and the other three entities were incorporated between 2023 and 2024.Once the freeze is executed and Sanpals are informed about the FIU directive, financial institutions and VASPs have to ask the account owners to provide documents that prove transaction legitimacy and lawful origin of funds.The inclusion of VASPs in the notice assumes significance given the legal acceptance and wide use of cryptocurrencies in UAE -- covering even transactions like property deals. VASPs include crypto exchanges, wallet providers, and entities offering trading, transferring, or digital asset safekeeping.The banks and VASPs will have to cancel the freeze after 30 days from the receipt of the notice if they do not receive any instruction from FIU to extend the freeze.Under UAE anti-money laundering legislation and recent frameworks like UAE FIU Regulation No (1) of 2026, financial institutions as well as VASPs are designated "reporting entities" obligated to share information and comply with FIU orders.A school dropout from Jabalpur who claims to have made big in Dubai, Sanpal has till now denied various media allegations about his activities and transactions. In May the Delhi High Court had said that media had "prematurely labelled" him as a culprit though the official investigation was not over.Sanpal could not be contacted for the story. ET's email and messages on his social media accounts did not elicit any response till the time of going to Press. It could not be determined whether he was in UAE.Interestingly, in the FIU notice, Satish's nationality is mentioned as Vanuatu - a South Pacific island nation that in the last few years has emerged as the quickest and cheapest route to switch citizenship and grab a new passport. Tabinda, 39, however, has a UK nationality, according to the notice.The nature of the information that the FIU may be possessing is not known, and under the UAE law, extending the freezing order beyond 30 days require an explicit order from the Attorney General. The need to wait for information from other jurisdictions and foreign FIUs can be cited as one of the reasons for extension.However, during the 30 days which ends around mid-August, banks and VSPs can only allow deposit of funds in any form (cash, money transfers, cheques etc) without letting any withdrawal or transfer. Indeed, withdrawal of cryptocurrencies and moving them to private wallets held in other countries is often seen as an easy may to move money across borders, bypassing banking channels.

articles.title: Here's how engineers plan to save the satellite sent to save NASA's Swift mission
articles.text:
One week ago, more than 200 miles above the Earth, a refrigerator-size satellite making its way toward an attempted rescue of NASA's $500 million Swift gamma-ray observatory suddenly spun out of control.

It didn't look good. The spacecraft, named Link, was rotating on multiple axes, rendering it unable to maintain a reliable communications link with the ground and complicating efforts to arrest the spin. Two of the satellite's three reaction wheels, used for pointing, also stopped working. Through sporadic radio contact, engineers discovered a problem with some of the spacecraft's cold gas thrusters used for finer attitude control.

The Link satellite is built, owned, and operated by Katalyst Space Technologies, a satellite servicing startup that won a $30 million contract from NASA to fly up to the Swift observatory, grab onto it, and boost its orbit before succumbing to aerodynamic drag and burning up int he atmosphere.

Review: Yes, we're still arguing about Nolan's The Odyssey
articles.text:
Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey has been a lightning rod for controversy ever since the first casting and design reveals, igniting afresh with each new trailer. The film has garnered plenty of well-deserved accolades (and earnings) since its release, and yet somehow the debates rage on between classicists and the general public alike—all this over an adaptation of an epic poem that's been around since roughly the 8th century BCE.

My take: the IMAX scale might be epic, but Nolan gives the story an intimate feel, weaving a captivating, nearly three-hour cinematic spell. While the magic slowly starts to dissipate once one leaves the theater, the powerful imagery will resonate for days. And the film gave me, personally, a fresh perspective on the central character of Odysseus.

articles.title: In Delhi, an emotional farewell to former Army chief Gen VN Sharma with full state honours
articles.text:
New Delhi: Former Chief of Army Staff General (Retd) Vishwa Nath Sharma was laid to rest with full military honours at a cremation ground in Delhi Cantonment area Saturday, day after he died at the age of 97.
The first President’s commissioned officer to become the Army chief, General Sharma had an illustrious military career. He was commissioned into the Armoured Corps’ 16th Light Cavalry, and led the Indian Army through a period of turbulence marked by insurgency in Punjab and deployment of the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) in Sri Lanka. He served as the 14th Chief of Army Staff from 1 May 1988 to 30 June 1990.
The three service chiefs—General Dhiraj Seth, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan and Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh paid tribute to General Sharma at the cremation.
Also in attendance were former Army chiefs—General (Retd) J.J. Singh, General (Retd) Deepak Kapoor, General (Retd) Dalbir Singh Suhag, General (Retd) M.M. Naravane, General (Retd) Upendra Dwivedi, and General (Retd) V.K. Singh—and former Chief of Defence Staff General (Retd) Anil Chauhan. Former Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal (Retd) Nirmal Suri and Lieutenant General Ajay Ramdev, Director General Integrated Training, were also present.
Hailing from an illustrious military family, General Sharma was the son of late Major General Amar Nath Sharma. His eldest brother, late Major Som Nath Sharma, is the first recipient of the posthumous Param Vir Chakra. His sister was Major Dr Kamla Tewari, who served in the Army Medical Corps. His other brother, Lt Gen Surinder Nath Sharma, who retired as the Engineer-in-Chief of the Army, was also present at the funeral. He is now 103 years old.
General Sharma’s daughters performed his last rites, accompanied by the 17-gun military salute. Many of his friends were also present to pay their respects.
Air Chief Marshal (Retd) Nirmal Suri, who was a friend of General Sharma’s at the Royal Indian Military College—now the Rashtriya Indian Military College (RIMC)—in Dehradun, called him a “natural charmer”.
“His contributions to the Indian armed forces are immense. The country should learn from him and I think future generations will emulate him,” he remarked.
R.S. Bhatti, a former squadron leader of the Indian Air Force and alumnus of Sherwood College that General Sharma had also attended, said, “I followed in his footsteps. I am much, much junior to him. He is revered both at Sherwood and RIMC. RIMC is hard to get into… but it is a great path to follow… He was extremely sharp, mentally, just like his brother… very well informed. It was always a pleasure talking to him.”
Chiranjit Banerjee, trustee of the Rimcollian Old Boys Association, remembered General Sharma as an “extremely witty individual who would hold a gathering in absolute thrall” with his sense of humor. Banerjee said, “He wore his rank very lightly, and yet commanded massive respect due to his humane persona.”
During his 38 years of distinguished service, Gen Sharma held important commands, staff and instructional appointments. As a Major, he saw action during the 1965 India-Pakistan War in the Lahore sector. As a Lieutenant Colonel, he commanded the 66 Armoured Regiment and was later appointed an instructor at the Defence Services Staff College, Wellington. He was Col. General Staff Operations of an Armoured Division on the Western Front during the 1971 India-Pakistan War. Gen Sharma took over as General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Eastern Command in June 1987. As the Eastern Army Commander, his tenure witnessed a standoff with China at Sumdorong Chu along the Line of Actual (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh.

articles.text:
A local judge has ruled that Waymo can no longer use its side-by-side charging facilities overnight in Santa Monica, California, as these may pose a “public nuisance.”

Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Bradley S. Phillips granted this week the City of Santa Monica’s motion for a preliminary injunction in the city’s ongoing public nuisance lawsuit against the autonomous vehicle giant.

City officials and neighbors assert that the constant stream of vehicles at the charging stations create light and sound pollution and cause undue traffic congestion on the streets and nearby alleys, creating a collective bother and disruption.
